title: Demystifying Reasoning Dynamics with Mutual Information
one_line_claim: Large reasoning models exhibit detectable peaks in mutual information at specific 'thinking tokens' that are critical for reasoning quality and can be leveraged for inference optimization.
method_summary: Measures mutual information (via Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion) between token representations and correct answers across LRM reasoning trajectories. Identifies thinking tokens as those exhibiting sharp MI peaks; analyzes their prevalence on MATH, GSM8K, AIME24. Proposes Representation Recycling and Thinking Token-based Test-time Scaling.

key_findings.finding: Thinking tokens (e.g., 'Hmm,' 'Wait,' 'Therefore') exhibit sharp MI peaks and are predominantly reflective expressions marking transitions in reasoning logic.
key_findings.quote: These tokens often express reflections ('Hmm,' 'Wait'), transitions ('Therefore,' 'Thus'), or conclusions ('So,' 'Hence') -- intuitively representing significant points in the reasoning trajectory

key_findings.finding: Suppressing thinking tokens degrades performance: GSM8K 72.7% -> 51.3%, MATH500 33.7% -> 17.6%, AIME24 33.3% -> 16.7%.
key_findings.quote: Suppressing thinking tokens: GSM8K (72.7% -> 51.3%), MATH500 (33.7% -> 17.6%), AIME24 (33.3% -> 16.7%)

key_findings.finding: Theorem 1: expected prediction error is bounded by 1-MI(s;Y), so maximizing MI minimizes error.
key_findings.quote: E[L(Y,Y_hat)] <= E[1 - MI(s;Y)] where s is the hidden state and Y is the target

relation_to_herald.shared: Both analyze per-token signals during LLM generation to assess quality and operate at inference time without retraining.
differs_on: This paper studies normal reasoning dynamics; HERALD predicts compression-induced catastrophic failures (looping, non-termination).
This paper uses mutual information / representation-space analysis; HERALD uses logit-space features with XGBoost.
This paper proposes training-free optimization (TTTS, Representation Recycling); HERALD requires a trained XGBoost predictor.
